headline_marked: Tawhid Hridoy sets [[highest individual Test score for Bangladesh]] in Sylhet
headline: Tawhid Hridoy sets highest individual Test score for Bangladesh in Sylhet
summary: Hridoy smashed an unbeaten 223 against West Indies, surpassing Mushfiqur Rahim's long-standing record of 219.
details: Tawhid Hridoy has rewritten the record books by scoring the highest individual Test score for Bangladesh. He remained unbeaten on 223 off 340 balls, featuring 22 fours and 10 sixes, during the second Test against West Indies in Sylhet.

Hridoy surpassed Mushfiqur Rahim's previous record of 219 not out against Zimbabwe in 2018. He also became the first Bangladeshi to convert his maiden Test century into a double-century, beating Mominul Haque's 181.

The batter set a new national record for the most sixes in a Test innings with 10, overtaking Tamim Iqbal's previous record of seven. He also registered the highest individual score ever recorded at the Sylhet International Cricket Stadium.

Hridoy's historic knock helped Bangladesh recover from a precarious 184-7 to reach 356-8, drawing level with the West Indies' first-innings total. He shared a record-breaking 117-run eighth-wicket partnership with Taijul Islam.

This performance marks a massive turnaround for Hridoy, whose previous best in four Test innings was only 42. He had faced criticism after the previous Test in Mirpur and only featured in the XI due to Mominul Haque's absence.

headline_marked: Summit [[LNG terminal resumes supply]] after maintenance
headline: Summit LNG terminal resumes supply after maintenance
summary: Operations at the Moheshkhali terminal have returned to normal, restoring gas flow to the national grid after a scheduled emergency maintenance period.
details: Gas supply from Summit's liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal in Moheshkhali has resumed following scheduled emergency maintenance.
Petrobangla confirmed on Saturday that the terminal began regasifying imported LNG at 1pm, restoring full operations for the national grid.
The maintenance period lasted from November 4 to November 7, during which Petrobangla forecast a daily supply drop from 2,570 to 2,250 million cubic feet (mmcfd).
Before the shutdown, the state-run agency dismissed social media claims that gas supply across the country would be completely suspended for four days.
Bangladesh operates two floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) in Moheshkhali: one operated by Summit Group and another by US-based Excelerate Energy.
Summit's terminal has a regasification capacity of 500mmcfd, while Excelerate Energy's can handle 600mmcfd, totaling a combined capacity of 1,100mmcfd.
caption:
Gas supply is back to normal! Summit's LNG terminal in Moheshkhali has resumed operations after emergency maintenance.

Gas supply from Summit's liquefied natural gas (LNG) terminal in Moheshkhali has resumed following scheduled emergency maintenance.

Petrobangla confirmed on Saturday that the terminal began regasifying imported LNG at 1pm, restoring full operations for the national grid.

The maintenance period lasted from November 4 to November 7, during which Petrobangla forecast a daily supply drop from 2,570 to 2,250 million cubic feet (mmcfd).

Before the shutdown, the state-run agency dismissed social media claims that gas supply across the country would be completely suspended for four days.

Bangladesh operates two floating storage and regasification units (FSRUs) in Moheshkhali: one operated by Summit Group and another by US-based Excelerate Energy.

Summit's terminal has a regasification capacity of 500mmcfd, while Excelerate Energy's can handle 600mmcfd, totaling a combined capacity of 1,100mmcfd.
